title: Banana Bread
subtitle: Moist loaf with very ripe bananas and brown sugar
excerpt: A dense, moist loaf made with very ripe bananas, soft brown sugar, and a little soured cream. The ripest bananas give the most flavour: black-skinned is ideal. Keeps well for four days.

recipe.sourceNotes: Banana bread became popular in the United States during the Great Depression as a way to use overripe bananas. It spread to Britain and became a home-baking staple, particularly popular during lockdown in 2020. The best banana bread uses bananas so ripe the skin is mostly black: the starch has converted to sugar and the flavour is intense. Soured cream or yoghurt keeps the crumb moist.

content.text: The riper the banana, the sweeter and more intense the bread. Bananas with black skins are not past it: they are at their best for baking. Do not over-mix the batter once the flour is added or the loaf will be tough. A skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean when the loaf is done.
Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Grease a 900 g loaf tin and line with baking paper.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl until smooth. Stir in the melted butter, brown sugar, eggs, soured cream, and vanilla extract.
Sift in the self-raising flour, bicarbonate of soda, and salt. Fold gently until just combined. Do not over-mix.

Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 50 to 55 minutes until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. If the top colours too quickly, cover loosely with foil after 35 minutes. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes before turning out.
